text.pt: — Porque andamos aos ziguezagues? — Contra o vento não se vai a direito, menina. Vira-se de bordo, de um lado e do outro. Olhe as fragatas e as faluas: o rio está cheio.
text.en: "Why do we keep zigzagging?" "You can't sail straight into the wind, miss. We tack, one side then the other. Look at the fragatas and faluas: the river's full."

text.pt: — E não podemos ir a direito? — Ao vento, não. Vai-se em ziguezague, à bolina de um bordo e do outro. Aquela falua também leva gente.
text.en: "Can't we just go straight?" "Not into the wind. We zigzag, close-hauled on one side, then the other. That falua carries people too."

text.pt: — Porque não larga isto? — É o rio que liga as duas margens, menina. — Então leve-me depressa: o meu irmão casa hoje.
text.en: "Why not give this up?" "It's the river that joins the two banks, miss." "Then hurry: my brother marries today."

evidence.paraphrase: Tacking: “virar de bordo” (en) — Tacking: turning through the wind to change sides while going upwind, zigzagging between two close-hauled headings.

The river was the era's motorway, busy with varied craft: fragatas, varinos, faluas, cangueiros, botes, botes de fragata, botes de pinho, barcos de água acima, canoas and catraios. · place: Tagus estuary
Faluas formed a fairly regular network carrying passengers; a children's rhyme about a falua from Belém survives. · place: Belém · cargo: people
Falua: “falua” (pt-PT) — Medium-sized Tagus boat between a bote and a large fragata, doing similar cargo work and also carrying passengers.
Historically the Tagus was the only road for national and intercontinental trade and linked the two banks; the crossing still carries this maritime heritage. · place: Tejo · cargo: trade

River traffic linked the two banks, coast and interior, and mouth and Riba-Tejo, carrying goods and people and supporting fishing, until the mid-20th century. · place: Tejo, Riba-Tejo · when: until meados do séc. XX · cargo: goods and people
